_meta.role: Machine Learning Engineer Graduate (Search Ads) - 2027 Start

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY with machine learning experience across NLP, Transformer architectures, and model optimization. Built a GPT-2 style language model and a sequence-to-sequence ASR system from scratch in PyTorch, including multi-head self-attention, cross-attention decoding, and a custom BPE tokenizer.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT, an OCR-free document understanding Transformer, for structured field extraction, improving validation accuracy from 55% to 93%.
Built PyTorch training pipelines on the Hugging Face VisionEncoderDecoder API with domain-specific tokens.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered a data pipeline for the multi-modal BraTS 2020 MRI dataset with augmentation and batch loading.
Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones; evaluated on Dice Score and IoU.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Curated a custom detection dataset and trained YOLOv8n on 1,133 images, achieving 83% mAP@50 on validation.
Exported trained models to ONNX and TFLite for deployment under memory and latency constraints.

projects.name: GPT-2 Style Language Model from Scratch
bullets: Implemented a GPT-2 style Transformer from scratch in PyTorch with multi-head self-attention and weight tying.
Built a TikToken-based tokenizer wrapper and a custom training loop with early stopping and perplexity evaluation.

projects.name: Sequence-to-Sequence ASR System from Scratch
bullets: Built an end-to-end seq2seq speech pipeline: 80-channel mel spectrogram encoder and 4-block causal Transformer decoder with cross-attention, reaching 15% WER on a Hindi-English dataset.
Designed a custom BPE tokenizer with a Cython-accelerated backend achieving 4-5.5x speedup over pure Python, processing 6M characters in 15 minutes.

projects.name: LLM Compression and Benchmarking
bullets: Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization (bitsandbytes LLM.int8()) on TinyLlama 1.1B; profiled peak VRAM and inference latency using pynvml.
Benchmarked across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC with under 1% accuracy degradation after compression.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Replaced TorchScript convolution layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing, constant memory for weights, and preallocated global buffers.
Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms versus 77.5ms CPU TorchScript, a ~35% speedup with identical accuracy.
